**Publish gate report: Chamomile and Lemon Balm product page**

**Going out:** Product page copy, Pebblebrook Tea Co. website, UK audience.

**Claims check**
| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "reduces anxiety" | Health claim. Banned by policy section 3. Remove. |
| "helps you sleep" | Health claim. Banned (health claims of any kind). Remove. |
| "Certified organic by the Soil Association" | On the policy list, exact wording. OK. |
| "20 plastic-free tea bags" | "Plastic-free" is on the policy list. The count of 20 is a product fact (cup counts), fine as written. OK. |
| "gentle, honeyed caffeine-free" | Flavour and ingredient description, product fact. OK. |

**Regulated claims:** "reduces anxiety" and "helps you sleep" are the risky lines. Both imply the tea treats a health condition or outcome, which is what advertising rules on health claims target. Safer version keeps the flavour and the evening-cup mood without promising an effect.

**House style:** No banned words. Voice is fairly warm and plain. Clean after the health fixes. Score about 88 before the fix, and the same after, since the rewrite only removes the claims.

**Disclosure:** Own product page, no partnership, affiliate link or gifted product. Nothing needed.

**Fixed (suggested rewrite, not yet approved):**
> Chamomile and Lemon Balm. A gentle, honeyed, caffeine-free blend for a quiet cup at the end of the day. Certified organic by the Soil Association. 20 plastic-free tea bags.

- Removed "reduces anxiety and helps you sleep".
- Added "a quiet cup at the end of the day" as a mood description, with no effect promised.

**Needs a decision:** None beyond accepting the rewrite. The original draft should not go out as written.

**Approver:** Sam (marketing lead). I need an explicit yes from Sam on the revised text above before publishing. No approval has been recorded, and nothing has been published.
